_what: REAL recorded output from the pinned Parakeet speech engine — not written by hand, not scripted. Each line is what the engine said when it was given the first N seconds of one real recording and asked, from scratch, what the whole thing says. That is exactly what voice-worker.ts does while somebody is talking (it re-hears the open stretch on every pass), so this file is the only evidence in the suite of how the real engine behaves — a hand-written fake always improves tidily and can never show the rewriting this whole grey-text rule exists to contain.
_machine: Linux x64, 4 decode threads, sherpa-onnx 1.13.7, sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8 (the pin in src/main/voice/voice-pin.ts)
_audio: jfk.wav — 11 s of a public-domain John F. Kennedy inaugural recording, 16 kHz mono, the sample shipped with whisper.cpp and used by the voice bench rig.
_command: node gen-rehear-ladder.js jfk.wav > parakeet-rehear-ladder.json   # engine + model set up per docs/active/prototypes/voice-stt-bench/README.md (youcoded-dev)
_generator: // Records a REAL Parakeet re-hear ladder: growing 1-second prefixes of one
// utterance, each decoded from scratch, exactly as voice-worker.ts's re-hear
// loop re-decodes the whole open segment on every pass.
transducer: { encoder: path.join(M, 'encoder.int8.onnx'), decoder: path.join(M, 'decoder.int8.onnx'), joiner: path.join(M, 'joiner.int8.onnx') },
st.acceptWaveform({ samples: wav.samples.slice(0, Math.round(n * sr)), sampleRate: sr });
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ audioSeconds: total, sampleRate: sr, passes }, null, 2));
_theRewrite: Look at 2 s -> 3 s. "And so my fellow American" becomes "And so, my fellow Americans." — a comma appears three words back, in text the engine had already said. Look again at 3 s -> 4 s and 9 s -> 10 s: the full stop the engine had written DISAPPEARS, so text that had turned solid goes back to grey. This is measured, it is the reason voice-types.ts refuses to promise that solid text never changes, and it is what voice-rehear.test.ts pins.
